item.title: Dansk pharmaceutical company stock drops after weight loss data
item.description: Shares of the Danish pharmaceutical company Zealand Pharma fell sharply after the company released new data for its weight loss drug Petrilintid. By 10 a.m., the stock was down 30 percent. The results from a phase 2 study, published Thursday evening, showed weight loss of up to 10.7 percent of body weight after 42 weeks. […]

item.title: Overwhelming interest in special flight from the Middle East
item.description: About 800 Danish citizens have asked for a seat on a special flight planned by Denmark’s Foreign Ministry to bring stranded people home from the Middle East. item.title: Danish far-right pary proposes facial recognition in ghetto areas
item.description: The Denmark Democrats want police to use facial recognition in areas with high crime and where many convicted criminals live. The proposal is part of ten measures on immigration the party presented on Friday. Under the plan, surveillance cameras will be installed in selected “ghetto areas.” Facial recognition would be used to help police investigate […]

item.title: Iceland to hold EU referendum on August 29
item.description: Iceland first applied for EU membership in 2009 under a center-left government, and negotiations began the following year. The process was stopped in 2013 when a more EU-skeptical government came to power.

item.description: Forget about MitID, Rejseplanen, and e-Boks: these are “entry-level” apps. Danes have many official ones you may not even know about.

item.title: Fewer people are moving to Copenhagen because of high housing prices
item.description: Since 2000, Copenhagen has gained 175,000 residents. The forecast shows the city is expected to grow by another 93,000 people by 2060, reaching a population of 765,000.

item.title: What internationals should know about neurodiversity, relocation, and life in Denmark
item.description: Relocation is also one of the most significant psychological stressors a person can experience. For neurodivergent individuals especially, moving country can quietly amplify challenges, write Kirsten Baldocchi and Sidsel Byskov Hansen
